saints.name: St. Rita of Cascia
saints.title: Religious
saints.shortBlurb: The wife, mother, and widow who became an Augustinian nun, honored as the saint of impossible causes…
biography: Born near Cascia in Umbria about 1381, Rita was given in marriage young to a harsh husband; she bore his ill temper with patience and, after his violent death, forgave his killers and prevented her sons from taking revenge. Widowed and then bereft of both sons, she sought entry to the Augustinian convent at Cascia and was at last admitted.

For forty years she lived in prayer and penance, receiving, it is said, a wound on her forehead as though from a thorn of Christ's crown. She died in 1457, and popular devotion made her the advocate of desperate and seemingly hopeless situations; she was canonized in 1900.
saints.knownFor: Patient endurance and intercession in impossible causes.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 22 May
